newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU deal could boost Ukrainian steel exports.
newsitem.headline: EU deal could boost Ukrainian steel exports.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it had reached a deal with Ukraine which would allow the former Soviet republic to boost sales to the European Union of some steel and iron products up to the year 2001.
It would be linked to the introduction of "normal competitive conditions" in Ukraine, especially in the areas of competition policy, state aid and environmental protection.

"This will ensure that Ukraine can enjoy stable growth for one of its major exports to the European Union while gradually bringing the competitive conditions of the Ukrainian steel industry more into line with those of the European Union," the EU executive said in a statement.
The deal, to replace one for 1995-1996, would be submitted to EU foreign ministers for approval and should enter into force on July 1.
It would cover certain iron and steel products, such as coils, heavy plate or wire rod.
Quotas would be adjusted to boost quantities for products which Ukraine can export and to reduce others which it cannot use fully, the Commission said.
The quantitative limits would increase by 10 percent to 233,154 tonnes for 1997 compared with the previous year, and rise by a further five percent in 1998 and 2.5 percent annually in 1999-2001.
In 1995 and 1996, Ukraine only used roughly half of its export limits for both years.
Total EU imports of Ukrainian iron and steel products, including those where trade has already been liberalised, rose to 1.6 million tonnes in 1995 from 660,000 tonnes in 1993.
The Commission said it and Ukrainian authorities planned to develop technical cooperation projects in order to support implementation of the agreement.

In October, the EU executive said it had been authorised to negotiate new five-year steel trade accords with Russia, Ukraine and Kazakhstan aimed at progressively opening up the EU to steel products from the three countries from 1997 to 2001.
However, Thursday's statement did not mention the status of talks with Russia and Kazakhstan.
The three countries exported to the EU about 7.2 million tonnes of steel and other ferrous products in 1995 while the EU exported to them about 175,000 tonnes. -- Brussels newsroom +32 2 287 68 11
